reviews.text: 很有创意很有想法的一个卡牌游戏，自己扮演的是一个火龙boss对抗人类军队，卡牌可以改变场地格子的地形，不同地形叠加会触发不同效果，一开始有点懵逼，慢慢上手以后感觉这游戏还真有点东西，期待正式版
题材挺新颖的，没想到攻击方式是改变地形，这点我挺喜欢的，而且魔王有3阶段，终于不是你扮演勇者被超强的魔王一拳打飞了，泪目了
第一次在卡牌游戏里当BOSS，挺有创意的。在卡牌的玩法上添加了类似棋盘的格子，不同的卡牌会对格子造成特定的元素效果，不同的元素之间还可以融合，非常有意思，等一手正式版吧

I would recommend if you are into tile based games. The idea is interesting. Needs some preview on special combinations you can do when you hover over them or something. There's a lot of builds you can try even now. It's a fun concept, hoping to see more of this.
许久没体验当boss的感觉了，上一次还是霸王系列，这个游戏的卡牌元素组合有点烧脑，配合不同地形可以玩出花，目前就是感觉难度有点太高了，身为boss没啥逼格，一个火球两点伤害，对面几百的血，看我一下六七十，希望正式版加强boss

游戏作为一个卡牌游戏，一反常态让玩家扮演boss去击败人类方的各路勇者：盗贼，法师，牧师，骑士等，让玩家体验一下当boss的爽快感。游戏核心玩法就是元素搭配造成不同效果，玩法比较丰富，风，土，火三类元素的combo让玩家能打出一些意想不到的独特效果，期待后续能够加入更多元素和初始玩家的属性，例如擅长毒类攻击的毒龙，风可以让毒池变为毒雾扩散，火能让毒雾产生爆炸，土能让毒池化为有毒土壤造成永久负面属性等等。如果属性多元化能够提上日程，相信这款游戏未来可期。
一开场，直接让我们作为对战勇者的恶龙出场还是挺新颖的，让人有种眼前一亮的感觉，这次该轮到我当恶龙了，游戏是卡牌对战游戏，玩法的核心机制是通过卡牌中的各种属性来产出化学反应从而打出1+1>2的效果，各种卡牌效果互相搭配从而改变地形产生各种化学反应。目前看游戏潜力巨大，期待正式版更新（我都成恶龙了，我抢的公主在哪呢，咳咳）

非常新奇的一个肉鸽赛道，这次你不再扮演屠龙的勇者，而是扮演真正的巨龙去摧毁城镇占领地区； 游戏围绕场地效果展开战斗，玩家作为巨龙要利用风岩火三种属性卡牌配合改变场地、对抵抗的人类造成伤害；游戏中有一个元素反应表格专供玩家随时查看，在合适的时机和地点善用不同的卡牌可以造成连锁反应级的爆炸效果； 但是目前游戏的进度以及数值平衡似乎欠佳，对于局外成长的依赖性非常高，但前期局外成长低导致局内过关极少，结算经验很低，局外成长缓慢形成恶性循环； 即使玩家熟悉卡组优势以后也几乎难以完成50%的关卡，敌人的数值变化卡稳了玩家的任何组合，在占三图第二突击队这个节点上一旦刷到稻草人几乎就是死局；一百攻击对玩家就是摸两下即死，更别提半场加速，如果没有龙卷风后推，六回合必死。
woc！元素反应！需要时间来拉数值的卡牌游戏，我TM一条龙打不过哥布林：）
很好玩的卡牌游戏有点像杀戮尖塔，不过这次我们当的boss，一开始肯定打不过死多了升级了关键技能就很好过了，很有意思的游戏。期待正式版。

The game mechanics seem raw and rely on the RNG of getting cards worth using. The game is non-optimized as hell. For some reason it chugs the most when returning to the main menu. Pretty basic and meh content-wise. The gameplay is constantly limited by what you are not allowed to have and an artificial need to grind and fail until you have enough experience to unlock the cards worth using. You are not playing to advance in the game and rather are held back by the lack of tools to artificially lengthen the game while not being given much content to enjoy. It is an extremely obvious game development scheme of trying to invest as little time on creating assets as possible. That also means there is almost nothing to see and play the game for.

The game is fun but man it can be quite hard. With some enemies made directly to counter you. Builds are a little RNG and meteors for being a rather pushed mechanic, only seem to serve to ruin your setup ngl. Update: Having played a up to 9 hours now and the game has me hooked. I hope more cards and builds come around, some of the Boss phase mechanics are better and synergies well with others. Once you learn how to setup decent area control and how to counter certain heroes such as the barrel goblin and smileman you will get a lot further. I just wish my unlocks would carry over, but maybe I've just sunk too much time into a demo XD. The concept is awesome, hopefully cosmetics and different bosses will be added. Additional exhale cards with different shapes would be nice also.

The premise of the game is an interesting one, instead of the hero, you are the raid boss and fight them. Interesting enough for me to try the demo, since I am usually not that into deckbuilder games, but the “playing the dragon” component had me curious enough. I’d like to point out that the majority of my playtime was done before the “big patch”, but frankly the big patch did not really change much. Where before there where simple two digit numbers to deal with, they blew them up now with adding two zeros to make the game seem more big and epic, but frankly the numbers are just annoying now, not to even speak that the majority of the tooltips are still not updated and still show the old values. Also it made the game way too easy, now you can stand just idly there and do nothing, and the heroes barely make a dent to your health, when before you had to think and weigh your options just to survive. The artstyle seems okay enough, but the sound design is from abysmal to non-existent, there is barely any sound clues for anything, aside from obvious stock sounds. The animations are extremely barebones, if there are any. Often the UI glitches and does not react to commands, or selects the wrong tile on the field. The game seems also very sloppily programmed, it takes very long to boot up, too long for a 2D rouge like deckbuilder. All of the animations lag the first time they are played in a session, a clear sign that everything needs to be shoveled into the RAM first before the animations play. Why does the game take so long to load if the animations are not loaded in at the startup? Also the game takes up whopping 2 GB of storage on your harddrive, way more compared to a full release game like Banners of Ruin (+Add-Ons, which takes up around 1,4 GB of storage). Devs in general need to learn to package and shrink their file sizes down and not treat disk storage as free real estate. Also it does not make it better that the achievement „liquid fire“ is bugged, not even speaking off the 8 achievements that have placeholder names and are not even assigned, so it is impossible to 100% the prologue. The game does overall feel very sloppy and unfinished, even for a demo or „prologue“, as they call it. For a free demo it is fine, but I don’t really have much hope for the full release if the devs think such a buggy mess will people will draw into the paid game. It is a shame, because the “being the raid boss” angle is quite interesting to be honest.

And you can tell that the "00" is stapled onto the end of everything to make things feel bigger, but they dont matter, and in particular, several cards/relics/powers/the tutorial still refer to things in single/double digits instead of quadruple/quintuple. As it is now, Im not interested at all, and I think this needs HEAVILY refined before it goes onwards.

The demo for this game shows a lot of potential, but it’s clear that it needs significant refinement before it can fully deliver on its promise. As the "legendary dragon" protagonist, players are left feeling underwhelmed. The gameplay feels weak and lacks depth, with limited animations and uninspired mechanics that don’t evoke the sense of power you'd expect from such a legendary creature. In fact, the experience sometimes feels like you’re playing an elemental wizard rather than a fearsome dragon. Despite the underwhelming dragon experience, there are moments of fun to be had. The game offers a unique card system with satisfying combos that will keep players engaged. For fans of turn-based strategy or RPGs, the concept of playing as the final boss is intriguing, and there’s a certain charm in the way the mechanics unfold. The game shows promise in how it integrates terrain effects and tactical interactions, even if they aren’t fully realized yet. Overall, this demo is a mixed bag: fun and full of potential, but definitely in need of further polish. Fans of turn-based strategy and card games might still find it worth keeping an eye on, but the game will need to address its bugs, improve its pacing, and refine its core gameplay to truly shine in the final release.

"None Shall Intrude: Descent" is is not a game. It's an advertisement for a product called "None Shall Intrude". None Shall Intrude is a glorified browser CCG that's riddled with bugs and abandoned by the developers who moved on to other projects. No wonder GrabTheGames saw that garbage and had to put their name on it as a publisher. But this isn't completely relevant because this is not None Shall Intrude, it's just an advertisment for it, so it's not correct to try to review that completely distinct product. We must instead review this for what it is... an advertisement. If you enjoy advertisements, you can consume them for free on the web or on Youtube without needing to add them to your game library, download them, and then launch the advertising. It's impossible in a general sense to recommend people should do that over playing real, full games on Steam, and that applies here with "None Shall Intrude: Descent" too. The goal here is to get you to spend [b]$15 USD[/b] on [i]None Shall Intrude[/i]. I don't recommend you get suckered, or reward these kinds of shady, deliberately misleading marketing practices. They're harmful to everyone. Now onto pricing and value. As an advertisement, this is only free in the same way that adverts on Youtube and banner ads in your browser are. This is a game demo that's been dumped on Steam to advertise another Steam store page in the hopes of raking in some cash. Just because advertisements are free, doesn't mean they're worth your time. It's important to understand there's a formal process to create a demo/page for a game which hasn't been followed here: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/application/demos While it might seem like an innocuous mistake, publishing demos and advertisements as if they are full games is misleading and in some ways harmful. This advertisement is taking up marketing space and visibility that would be better made available to a developer that's done the right thing and created a full game. Instead, that visibility is given over to a demo/advert that's been published incorrectly and is polluting the marketplace. It's unclear if this mistake was made through incompetence or a deliberate intent to mislead gamers. Often developers may choose to incorrectly publish demo/advertisements as separate games as a cheap way to bypass paying Valve for marketing presence on the Steam front page, which may seem clever to them, but it's harmful behaviour and it's not good for gamers. Advertisements and incorrectly published demos don't add +1 to your game collector count, they aren't full games. It's impossible for me to recommend this incorrectly published advertising spam to gamers, you deserve better than adverts.

Honestly, there aren't many roguelike card games where you get to be the bad guy. This one lets you play as a dragon out to conquer human lands, and that "finally I'm the villain" vibe is a lot of fun. The gameplay mixes strategy and luck pretty well. You can't just spam cards; you have to think about your hand and also pay attention to the terrain, because different elements can interact with each other in clever ways. And as your health drops, your dragon evolves into stronger forms, which adds a nice risk‑reward twist. It starts tough, but once you unlock a few upgrades, you really feel the power spike. If you're tired of always saving the world as the hero, give this a shot. You don't need to master all the mechanics upfront; just the thrill of being the one in control and wrecking stuff is worth it on its own
